PA MHAD privacy policy

Last updated: November 2026 (v1.4). The same policy is shown in the app under Settings → Privacy policy.

Data we collect

This app collects only the information you enter into your Mental Health Advance Directive forms, including:

  • Personal information (name, address, phone, date of birth)
  • Agent and witness information
  • Treatment preferences and medication lists
  • Digital signatures
  • Additional instructions

We do not collect analytics, crash reports, device identifiers, or location data.

How data is stored & protected

Your directive data is NOT transmitted to the app developer or any third party for storage.

This is a web app: your data is held in your browser tab. When you start, you choose whether to keep a copy on this device. If you do, it is locked with a passphrase only you know (AES-256 encryption) and expires 30 minutes after you leave; an expired copy is erased the next time the app is opened in this browser. If you don’t, your work is erased when you close the tab. Nothing is written to a server. Download your progress, or export or print your directive, to keep a copy.

AI features & third-party data sharing

The AI help is optional, and this app never sends anything to an AI service itself. If you choose to use it, the app writes instructions that you copy and paste into an AI chat service you choose — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok — and you attach any document or recording there yourself. You then copy the answer back into this app.

What you paste or attach in that service is handled under that service’s own terms and privacy policy, not this one. Depending on the service and your settings, it may:
Most services offer a private or temporary chat that keeps less — see “Outside AI services” below.

  • Keep your conversations, with or without an automatic expiration
  • Use them to improve its products
  • Let human reviewers read them

The instructions this app writes leave out common identifying details (SSNs, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, addresses, names, and facility names). This is a best-effort filter and cannot guarantee complete removal. A document or recording you attach yourself reaches the service as it is.

AI help is entirely optional. The app is fully functional without it.

Outside AI services

If you use an outside AI service with this app, be aware of the following:

1. That service decides how long it keeps what you send, and whether people or its AI models learn from it. Review its privacy policy and settings before you send sensitive content.

2. Data you send to that service cannot be recalled or deleted by this app. Once sent, it is under that service’s control.

3. For more privacy, use a private chat: ChatGPT’s Temporary Chat, Claude’s Incognito chat, Gemini’s Temporary chat, or Grok’s Private Chat.

You can avoid all third-party data sharing by not using the AI help.

International users (GDPR)

If you are in the European Economic Area (EEA), the UK, or Switzerland, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) may give you rights over your data. Here is how to use them in this app.

Legal basis for processing: Your explicit consent, given through the in-app disclaimer and the notice shown before you first copy anything to an outside AI service.

Your rights:

  • Right to access: Your data stays in your browser — you can see all of it in the app at any time.
  • Right to erasure: Use “Start over” to erase everything in this browser, including a locked copy kept on this device; “Delete saved progress” erases just the locked copy.
  • Right to data portability: Export your directives as PDF or FHIR JSON (a standard health-records format) at any time.
  • Right to withdraw consent: Stop using the AI help at any time — this app never sends anything to an AI service itself.
  • Right to restriction: When you start, choose to keep nothing outside the browser tab.

Data you paste or attach in an outside AI service is processed under that service’s own privacy policy and data processing terms. We cannot control or delete it once it has been sent.

US state health-privacy laws (CA, WA, CT, NV)

This app may be subject to state consumer-health-data privacy laws such as Washington’s My Health My Data Act (MHMDA), Connecticut’s CTDPA health provisions and Nevada’s SB 370. California’s CCPA/CPRA treats health information as “sensitive personal information”.

Mental-health-directive content is health data under each of these laws (“consumer health data” in Washington, Connecticut and Nevada; “sensitive personal information” in California). Under all of them: (1) We collect mental-health treatment-preference data solely to help you create your advance directive. (2) We do not sell your health data — there is no commercial recipient. (3) This app never sends your directive to a third party. The only things it sends are the lookups you start — a medication or condition name, a doctor’s name, or a ZIP code — to the services listed under “No third-party tracking”. If you choose to use the AI help, you copy instructions into an outside AI service yourself; that service receives only what you paste or attach there. (4) We use no analytics, advertising or tracking code, no tracking pixels and no cookies. (5) You can erase everything in this browser at any time with “Start over”, which also erases a locked copy kept on this device.

Washington MHMDA includes a private right of action; we have designed the app so that it never transfers your directive to a third party itself, and so that, before you first copy anything to an outside AI service in a session, it shows a notice explaining that the service’s own terms apply.

For questions about your privacy rights, contact the developer using the channels listed in the Contact section below.

Medical reference lookups (U.S. government data)

To help you fill in and understand your directive, the app looks things up in free, public U.S. government databases. These lookups use ONLY the single term or code needed for that lookup. They never receive your identity (your name, date of birth, address, or phone), the people you name (agents, witnesses, guardian), or your saved directive.

What is sent, and to whom:

  • Medication name you type → NLM RxTerms (autocomplete).
  • Condition name you type → NLM ICD-10-CM (diagnosis lookup).
  • A doctor / provider name you type into the optional doctor search → NLM NPI registry, used only to look that provider up in the public registry of healthcare providers.
  • A condition (by its ICD-10 code) or a medication (by name, resolved to a code via NLM RxNav) → NLM MedlinePlus Connect, to fetch a plain-language explanation.
  • A medication name → openFDA (U.S. Food & Drug Administration), to fetch that drug’s official FDA label, which is used to ground the side-effects list.

Each request contains only what you typed into that search, or the code it found — nothing else from your directive.

NLM, NIH, and the FDA are not responsible for this product and do not endorse or recommend it. These services are for information only and are not medical advice — consult a qualified professional. The NLM Clinical Table services are rate-limited to 20 requests/second.

Sources: U.S. National Library of Medicine (RxTerms, ICD-10-CM, NPI registry, RxNav, MedlinePlus Connect); U.S. Food & Drug Administration (openFDA).

PDF export & sharing

When you export a PDF of your directive, it is generated locally on your device. Sharing the PDF (via email, messaging, etc.) sends it through your device’s standard sharing mechanism. The app cannot control where the PDF is stored once shared.

Your rights

You can delete any directive at any time from the home screen. Deleting a directive removes all its data (personal information, agents, medications and treatment choices) from this browser tab.

To erase a locked copy kept on this device right away, choose “Delete saved progress” or “Start over”, or clear this site’s data in your browser settings.

Conversations in an outside AI service are kept or deleted with that service’s own controls.

No third-party tracking

This app does not include any third-party analytics SDKs, advertising frameworks, crash reporting services (such as Firebase, Crashlytics, or Sentry), or tracking pixels.

The only outside connections this app makes are:

  • Google’s servers (www.gstatic.com, fonts.gstatic.com) — each time the app loads, for its display engine and some fonts. Nothing you type is sent, but Google sees your IP address, as with any website that uses its fonts.
  • NIH/NLM Clinical Table Search Service — medication, condition, and provider (doctor) lookups
  • NLM MedlinePlus Connect & RxNav — plain-language condition and medication explanations (sends only an ICD-10 code or a medication name)
  • openFDA / U.S. FDA — official drug labels used to ground the side-effects list (sends only a medication name)
  • Zippopotam.us and the U.S. FCC’s Area API — only when you tap to fill city, county and state from a ZIP code (sends the ZIP code, then that area’s map coordinates)
  • Your browser’s speech recognition — only if you use voice dictation; browsers such as Chrome and Edge send the recording to their maker’s servers to turn it into text.

Each lookup receives only what you typed into that search, or the code or ZIP code being looked up — never your directive. The app never connects to an AI service: when you use the AI help, you open that service yourself. No data is sent to the app developer at any time.

HIPAA & compliance

This app is NOT HIPAA-compliant. It is not a covered entity or business associate under HIPAA. The app is intended for personal use by individuals preparing their own mental health advance directives.

While this app implements privacy measures aligned with GDPR, CCPA, and MHMDA principles (as described above), it has not been independently audited or certified for compliance with these regulations. If you require verified regulatory compliance, consult with a privacy professional before use.

Breach notification

In accordance with the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule, if a security breach exposes your health information, we will give notice within 60 calendar days of discovering it. Because the app collects no contact details, that notice is an in-app notice plus a notice posted on the hosted privacy policy page for at least 90 days.

This app keeps your directive in your browser and has no server-side database, so a breach would most likely involve the code the app is served from or one of the outside services named in this policy. If one of them notifies us of a breach affecting data sent through the app, we will pass that notification along in the same way.

Contact

Under the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule, notice goes by mail or email — or, when there are no contact details, as here (the app collects none), by a substitute notice posted for 90 days. We provide:

  • In-app: a breach notice shown the next time you open the app if a breach affects you.
  • Online: https://onica5000.github.io/MHAD/privacy.html (where the substitute notice is posted for at least 90 days).
